title: John Steele, Adventurer
paragraphs: An adventure anthology built around the far-traveled John Steele, whose work and wanderings carry him through jungles, deserts, ports, mysteries, and dangerous situations around the world.

Weekly Mutual adventure/thriller built around globe-trotting John Steele. The frozen GRH snapshot contains 49 distinct surviving recordings from a much longer 1949-56 run; three preserved titles remain undated and late copies include AFRTS rebroadcast forms.
GRH documents the program through Mutual network run (April 26, 1949 to July 16, 1956) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Don Douglas (performer on 49 recordings), Doc Whipple (performer on 13 recordings), Robert Monroe (producer on 12 recordings), Elliott Drake (director on 11 recordings and writer on 11 recordings), Ross Martin (performer on 11 recordings), Ted Mallie (announcer on 10 recordings), and Sylvan Levin (conductor on 7 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include dangerous adventure and pursuit, global travel and remote locations, ships, sea travel and maritime danger, expedition, wilderness and exploration, crime, captivity and violence, and sports and competition.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Long-running Mutual adventure programming, Postwar global-adventure radio, AFRTS rebroadcast preservation, and Atmospheric adventure scoring.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (8 shared credited people), [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (5 shared credited people), [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (5 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (5 shared credited people), and [[show|dimension-x|Dimension X]] (4 shared credited people).
